title: Microsoft Fabric Data Agent: Setup and Integration Guide
summary: A community/blog step-by-step walkthrough of building and publishing a Fabric data agent, largely restating Microsoft Learn's setup guide but adding specifics on how a published agent is consumed outside the Fabric chat UI — its callable API endpoint shape, the named Microsoft Foundry integration tool, Copilot Studio/Teams consumption paths, and available client SDK languages.
audience: Builders who have already read Microsoft's own data-agent docs and want a single narrative walkthrough of wiring a published agent into Foundry, Copilot Studio, or Teams rather than a UI-only workflow.
why_it_matters: The knowledge base's existing data-agent sources (from Microsoft Learn) cover configuration, governance, and evaluation in depth but say little about how an already-published agent is consumed as an API by external orchestrators; this post's Foundry tool name and endpoint/identity shape point to a concrete Microsoft Learn integration page worth ingesting directly.
takeaways: A published data agent exposes a callable API endpoint identified by a workspace_id and artifact_id pair, which is how external orchestrators (rather than the Fabric chat UI) invoke it.

Microsoft Foundry consumes a Fabric data agent through a named tool, MicrosoftFabricAgentTool, and per the post this integration requires the Foundry project and the Fabric workspace to be in the same tenant.
Client SDKs for calling a published data agent are listed as Python, TypeScript, and JavaScript.

The post caps example queries per data source at 100, a different (larger) number than any single-agent-wide limit discussed in the existing configuration source, and worth confirming against Microsoft Learn.

claims.text: A published Fabric data agent exposes a callable API endpoint identified by a workspace_id and an artifact_id, which is the mechanism external orchestrators use to invoke the agent outside the Fabric chat UI.

Microsoft Foundry integrates with a Fabric data agent through a named tool, MicrosoftFabricAgentTool, and per the post this requires the Foundry project and the Fabric workspace to be deployed in the same tenant.
The post lists Python, TypeScript, and JavaScript as the client SDK languages available for calling a published data agent's endpoint programmatically.
The post states a data agent can store up to 100 example queries per attached data source, a per-source cap distinct from the 5-data-source and 25x25-result limits described elsewhere.

Per the post, Copilot Studio consumes a data agent as a registered plugin and handles the conversational layer itself, while Microsoft Teams access to a data agent can go either directly through Fabric's own chat surface or indirectly via a Copilot Studio integration.

The post frames a data agent's 25-row/25-column response cap as a deliberate design choice for conversational use rather than a temporary limitation, explicitly recommending against relying on it for heavy analytical workloads.
